source.title: In Search of the Real Inductive Bias: On the Role of Implicit Regularization in Deep Learning
source.authors: Behnam Neyshabur; Ryota Tomioka; Nathan Srebro

record.tranche_reason: The paper directly sweeps hidden-layer width in one-hidden-layer ReLU networks and measures training and test error, matching V2's width-versus-generalization question.
record.gate_note: The paper reports results for width sweeps on natural labels, censored labels, and labels with 5 percent random noise. It also reports a weight-decay comparison. Figure values are not numerically legible in the supplied text, so values are recorded as figure only; the paper's explicit descriptions support the stated trends.
record.test_reason: This is the original source for V2. Its width sweeps measure training and test error in one-hidden-layer ReLU networks trained to convergence, and explicitly report decreasing test error beyond the width needed for zero training error.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is accurate: test error decreases beyond the width needed for zero training error, suggesting capacity control beyond network size. Optimization-induced complexity control, possibly involving norms, is proposed as an explanation rather than demonstrated. Explicit weight decay gives a slight additional improvement.
record.recipe_differences: This paper is the named original source for V2; it uses one-hidden-layer ReLU networks trained with SGD and momentum, without explicit regularization in the principal width sweeps.
record.method_sensitivity: The paper reports continuing test-error reductions on original, censored, and 5-percent-noisy label settings; it also reports a slight generalization improvement with explicit weight decay.

fits_no_version.finding: Validation-selected weight decay slightly improves generalization on the small natural-label datasets, while increasing width remains helpful.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Explicit weight decay can slightly improve held-out performance in these one-hidden-layer ReLU networks.

record.problems: The supplied figure text does not provide exact plotted error values. The artificial censored labels are constructed using a network trained on the entire dataset, including test and validation examples. Results in Figure 2 are averages over 5 repetitions, but no error bars are stated.

untested.parts: No fully random-label training condition or comparison of random-label held-out accuracy with chance; corrupting 5 percent of labels does not establish V1.
No convolutional versus fully connected comparison.
No adaptive optimizer versus SGD comparison.
No batch-size comparison under fixed epoch budgets.
No magnitude-aware sharpness measurement or comparison with generalization gaps.
No removal of examples selected by memorization.

missing.what: The authors report almost identical behavior when training with batch conjugate gradient descent. Add a qualitative optimizer-condition row; dataset-specific values and widths are not supplied.
missing.locator: Section 2, paragraph discussing convergence and implicit regularization

record.verdict_notes: No verdict labels are assigned because this study is V2's original source. The supplied text supports qualitative trends but does not expose plotted curve coordinates. The study does not establish a test-error peak near interpolation.

versions.untested_parts: Does not test fitting fixed random labels and comparing their held-out accuracy with natural-label accuracy.
Tests one-hidden-layer ReLU networks on MNIST and downsampled CIFAR-10; does not test other architectures, optimizers, or datasets.
No convolutional versus fully connected comparison.

source_check.notes: The inspected source is arXiv:1412.6614v4, dated 16 Apr 2015, by Neyshabur, Tomioka, and Srebro, with an ICLR 2015 workshop header; identity matches the recovered text. R1–R8 support qualitative trends only; plotted points can flatten or fluctuate, and exact test-error values are not stated. R9–R10 concern explicit weight decay, outside V2’s unregularized condition. The censored-label teacher was trained using the combined train, validation, and test data. No synthesis statements or verdict labels were included in this check.
